risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Management states PET production relies heavily on crude oil derivatives such as purified terephthalic acid (PTA) and monoethylene glycol (MEG), and that fluctuations in global crude oil prices and supply disruptions can directly impact production costs.
- Rapid advances in packaging and material science — including bio-based plastics, glass, aluminium and paper-based alternatives — may reduce demand for PET, and management notes that companies failing to upgrade manufacturing processes risk becoming less competitive.
- Management flags growing consumer and regulatory pressure to reduce single-use plastics, pushing for higher recycled content and lower PET usage, and warns that stricter plastic-waste disposal laws and extended producer responsibility (EPR) could raise compliance costs.
- Inadequate collection and recycling infrastructure in some regions limits recycled PET availability, affecting the ability to meet sustainability targets, while competition for high-quality rPET can increase input costs.
- Management states PET demand is closely tied to beverages, food packaging, textiles and industrial applications, so any slowdown in those sectors directly hits sales volumes.
- Tariffs, import restrictions or trade disputes can disrupt raw-material sourcing and finished-product exports, and management notes that dependence on specific countries for feedstock or machinery creates vulnerabilities.
- The Company states it operates in a single segment — PET preforms — in a market it describes as highly competitive, so there is no second business line to absorb pressure on the core product.
- The Board's realignment towards pharmaceuticals depends on identifying suitable opportunities and receiving all necessary statutory and regulatory approvals; the report states no new business operations have commenced as of its date, so the replacement revenue stream is an intention rather than an operating business.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strategic realignment out of PET/plastics: the Company is actively evaluating new business opportunities in the pharmaceutical sector to diversify revenue streams and leverage existing operational capabilities in what it calls a growing and resilient market.
- Explore pharmaceutical-sector entry across multiple routes — manufacturing, trading, marketing, contract manufacturing and other allied activities — conditional on identifying suitable opportunities and obtaining statutory and regulatory approvals.
- Keep the legal framework for diversification in place: shareholders approved an amendment …
